title: A frozen server clock must enter the observed writer
invariant: A local helper may freeze a server-issued clock only by injecting it into the observed writer the signer reads; freezing a quieter clock sibling such as Date.now or an inner Date constructor does not bind the request clock.

appliesWhen: a local helper freezes a server-issued clock before signing
the page exposes more than one clock-looking writer such as Date.now, ajax success, a rewritten getter, or an inner Date constructor
the request copies a clock field from the signer world
the clock may enter as a signer argument or query field rather than a rewritten getter
stopsWhen: the signer actually reads Date.now as the observed writer
the extra clock bytes never appear on the request
injecting the observed writer already binds the request clock

oracles.positive: python scripts/experience_fixture_check.py references/experience-fixtures/server-clock-observed-writer-matrix.json reports positiveOracle=true, injectsObservedWriter=true, and requestClockBound=true
oracles.negative: setting date-now-freeze-only.oracle=true or ajax-success-clock-inject.injectsObservedWriter=false while requestClockBound=true must fail the fixture checker

decision.action: inject the server-issued clock into the writer the signer reads, including a signer argument or query clock field; keep a Date.now or inner Date freeze only when that getter is the observed writer
decision.fallback: if the signer actually reads Date.now, freeze that getter; if the extra bytes never appear on the request, treat the clock as decoy
